data.title: Zvolen – Môťová, a Great Moravian hillfort in 3D
data.excerpt: The promontory hillfort of Priekopa once rose above the confluence of the Slatina and the Neresnica in what is today Zvolen, and counts among the local administrative centres of Great Moravia. Since the site was parcelled out among allotment gardeners after 1968 and devastated, we have reconstructed its Great Moravian appearance in 3D together with Dwarf digital archeology.

mediaTexts.alt: A 3D reconstruction of the hillfort with a stone-and-timber rampart and log houses above a lake

children.text: rose majestically in what is today Zvolen above the confluence of the small rivers Slatina and Neresnica, in the local district known as Môťová. We count the hillfort among the local administrative centres, that is among the more important hillforts of Great Moravia. During the Middle Ages it lost its importance and its function was taken over by Pustý hrad and later by Zvolen Castle.

In the 1930s the hillfort was surveyed by Štefan Janšák, and as late as the 1950s the hillfort was well preserved, even though a Roma settlement on its edge had begun to damage it. After 1968, however, by a decision of those in power at the time, the whole hillfort was parcelled out and handed over for use to 19 allotment gardeners. By failing to observe the principles of heritage protection, the gardeners devastated the hillfort completely, thereby robbing future generations of the very valuable information and finds that the hillfort held. The one exception is a single one of them, who at the beginning of the 1990s willingly allowed Dr Mácelová to carry out an archaeological excavation on his plot, and most of the known finds come precisely from that excavation. The others, however, were not so obliging. According to our information, one of the gardeners, who had the use of a peripheral part of the hillfort on which a stately building of the local chieftain in all probability stood, even had the soil with the remains of the stone and the material of the feature removed (carted away) to a depth of 100–120 cm and had other earth brought in, thereby destroying the whole feature. That is how some Slovaks value our history.

children.text: At present the hillfort is not marked in any way; the information panel that stands in the entrance gateway serves many purposes, but not that of providing information about the hillfort. The hillfort is fenced in, the gate closed, and only the allotment gardeners have access to it.
This is one of the reasons why we decided, together with

, to attempt to reconstruct the original appearance of the hillfort in the period of Great Moravia. For her expert advice we thank the archaeologist Marta Mácelová, who investigated the hillfort and who provided us with valuable information about its defences, its gateway and its internal buildings.

Anyone who knows the present state of the site may perhaps be surprised that in our visualisation the promontory is skirted by a river on both sides, since today only the Neresnica runs along the western side of the promontory. This state of affairs is, however, the result of the diversion of the bed of the Slatina, which took place only in the 20th century. Originally the Slatina wound around the eastern part of the promontory, which is clearly apparent not only on the Second Military Survey, but also on the orthophoto map from the 1950s. The eastern slope of the hillfort was steep and ran straight down into the bed of the Slatina, and this side of the hillfort therefore did not need pronounced defences.
We hope you will like the visualisation of the earliest Zvolen.
